standard_prerequisites: Elementary distinguished squares of algebraic spaces and the induction principle for quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes from Cohomology of Schemes
The filtration lemma producing the descending chain of opens with affine-at-closing etale maps, from Decent Spaces
The refinement lemma turning a non-affine leg into a chain of elementary distinguished squares with affine legs
core_obligations: Extend the property from affines to all representable quasi-compact quasi-separated etale objects via the scheme induction principle applied to unions W cup V
Set up the descending filtration of X from the decent spaces filtration lemma and run descending induction on p
Handle the possible non-affineness of V_p by decomposing it into finitely many affines and inserting the chain W_{p,i}
Verify each inserted pair is an elementary distinguished square with affine leg and inductively conclude
proof_roadmap: Prove the representable case by the scheme induction principle
Reduce the statement to X itself using representability on the small etale site
Run the descending induction along the filtration, splitting V_p into affines
Chain the elementary distinguished squares and finish the induction
difficulty_reason: The counted conclusion is an induction principle allowing properties of quasi-compact quasi-separated algebraic spaces to be checked on affines and elementary distinguished squares with affine legs (source lines 1562-1640, label lemma-induction-principle). The solver must transfer the scheme induction principle to representable etale objects, then repair the failure of the distinguished-square hypothesis on the standard filtration by inserting a finite chain built from an affine decomposition, checking each refined pair; the chain-refinement argument is the substantive step. Allowed background: the cited filtration and refinement lemmas, delivered as navigation pointers.
